title: YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It)
points: Don't build features or extension points for hypothetical future needs.
Build what is required now; refactor when the need is real.
trade: YAGNI is not "ignore good design". Keep code clean and easy to change; just don't implement unneeded features.
test: How does YAGNI differ from KISS?
answer: YAGNI is about scope: don't build unneeded features. KISS is about how you build what you do need: keep it simple.

questions.question: A requirement says "pay in SGD". A teammate adds multi-currency conversion and a plugin system for gateways. Which principle does this break?
questions.explanation: YAGNI: don't build features for hypothetical future needs. Add them when the need is real.
